lines.native: Hola, soy Marginalia. Esta es la historia de Journathan, el hombre de muchas lenguas. Su viaje a casa dura veinte años. I sell books only to readers who understand them. No spoilers; I have eaten those pages. The book is called The Journey. Possibly named after him. Scholarship remains divided, mostly because I ate the evidence. ¿Adónde va Journathan?
lines.translation: Hello, I’m Marginalia. This is the story of Journathan, the man of many tongues. His journey home lasts twenty years. I sell books only to readers who understand them. No spoilers; I have eaten those pages. The book is called The Journey. Possibly named after him. Scholarship remains divided, mostly because I ate the evidence. Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: At The Old Bookshop, a bookworm emerges from a chewed spine. She annotates your arrival with a small, doubtful tick.

lines.native: Un libro, sí, pero esa no es la respuesta. That names an object, not his destination. Reading comprehension: pending. Lee otra vez. ¿Adónde va Journathan?
lines.translation: A book, yes, but that is not the answer. That names an object, not his destination. Reading comprehension: pending. Read again. Where is Journathan going?
lines.narrative: Marginalia makes a small annotation beside your elbow. It does not appear to be a recommendation.

lines.native: Entiendes el destino, pero tu respuesta está en inglés. Necesito una respuesta en español. ¿Adónde va Journathan? Reading comprehension: promising; language compliance: pending. I sell books, not exemptions. Even the footnotes have standards.
lines.translation: You understand the destination, but your answer is in English. I need an answer in Spanish. Where is Journathan going? Reading comprehension: promising; language compliance: pending. I sell books, not exemptions. Even the footnotes have standards.
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the air beside you. Apparently, you have margins.

lines.native: Correcto: va a casa. Reading comprehension: approved. Your sleeve now has academic value. Escucha este pasaje: El Cíclope le pregunta su nombre. Journathan responde: «Mi nombre es Nadie.» The first recorded translation trick, according to a footnote I have not eaten. Yet. ¿Qué nombre le da Journathan al Cíclope?
lines.narrative: Marginalia marks your answer correct in the margin of your sleeve, then opens a book with suspiciously few margins remaining.

lines.native: Journathan es su nombre real, pero no es el nombre que da al Cíclope. Reading comprehension: pending. His actual name is not the trick; that would make this a very short book. ¿Qué nombre usa en el pasaje?
lines.translation: Journathan is his real name, but it is not the name he gives the Cyclops. Reading comprehension: pending. His actual name is not the trick; that would make this a very short book. What name does he use in the passage?
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small correction in the margin of your shadow. There is evidently room for improvement.

lines.native: ¡Correcto! Usa el nombre Nadie. Entiendes el pasaje; el libro es tuyo. Journathan quiere volver a casa, pero primero necesita un buen nombre falso. Reading comprehension: approved. No spoilers; the remaining pages are load-bearing.
lines.translation: Correct! He uses the name Nobody. You understand the passage; the book is yours. Journathan wants to return home, but first he needs a good false name. Reading comprehension: approved. No spoilers; the remaining pages are load-bearing.
lines.narrative: Marginalia slides the book across the counter and annotates your receipt: ‘Has read something.’ In this shop, that constitutes an honours degree.

lines.native: Hola, ¿quién está ahí? Familiar footsteps. Promising. No spoilers, please.
lines.translation: Hello, who is there? Familiar footsteps. Promising. No spoilers, please.
lines.narrative: At the Market Entrance, Marginalia rests with her eyes closed and The Journey shut on her finger, like an old dog guarding a familiar door. A bookmark would have lacked commitment.

lines.native: Te oigo, te oigo. Pero ¿quién está ahí? Your English arrived safely. This reading requires Spanish. Partial credit for presence.
lines.translation: I hear you, I hear you. But who is there? Your English arrived safely. This reading requires Spanish. Partial credit for presence.
lines.narrative: Marginalia keeps her eyes closed and her finger between the pages. The book has accepted this arrangement under protest.

lines.native: There you are. Full marks for presence. I have waited a very long time, among these pages, for someone to read with. Even my footnotes have stopped expecting visitors.
lines.translation: There you are. Full marks for presence. I have waited a very long time, among these pages, for someone to read with. Even my footnotes have stopped expecting visitors.
lines.narrative: Marginalia opens her eyes. She places a bookmark with the care usually reserved for stopping a century.

lines.native: Eso significa que no tengo compañía. Your sentence confirms the problem. Pero tú estás aquí, entre mis libros. Reading comprehension: pending. Please reconsider that interpretation.
lines.translation: That means I have no company. Your sentence confirms the problem. But you are here, among my books. Reading comprehension: pending. Please reconsider that interpretation.
lines.narrative: Marginalia pencils a small question mark beside you. The pencil has clearly done this before.

lines.native: Sí, no estoy sola. Tú estás aquí, y ahora podemos leer juntos. Reading comprehension: full marks. I shall refrain from annotating you. For now.
lines.translation: Yes, I’m not alone. You’re here, and now we can read together. Reading comprehension: full marks. I shall refrain from annotating you. For now.
lines.narrative: Marginalia lowers her pencil. For once, she leaves a perfectly good margin empty.
